Theme

Latin word

accipiō

accipiō, accipere, accēpī, acceptum

verb, third conjugation

take, catch (a ball thrown to one); get, receive; take (a remark) in a certain way; receive, get, accept; receive, entertain (a guest); suffer, receive (a wrong, a defeat, a loss)

In this lexicon

  • catch

    also used · classical · Andresian p. 20; Erasm. Coll., Lūsus puerīlēs (Pila)

  • get

    also used · classical · Traupman 320

  • interpretation

    also used · classical · Ter. Ad. 606: ad contumēliam omnia accipiunt magis; Ter. Eun. 875: in eam partem accipiōque

  • receive

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Att. 6.1.1: accēpī tuās litterās; Plin. Ep. 7.21.4: gallīnam ut ā tē missam libenter accēpī; Traupman 389

  • receive

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Fam. 9.26.3: nōn multī cibī hospitem accipiēs, multī jocī; Hor. S. 2.6.80–81: rūsticus urbānum mūrem mūs paupere fertur accēpisse cavō

  • suffer

    also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 5.56: accipere quam facere praestat injūriam; Traupman 186: clādem accipere, to suffer a defeat

Examples

  • accēpī tuās litterās …; quās lēgī libentissimē plēnissimās amōris

    I received your letter …, and read it with the greatest pleasure, so full of affection as it wasCic. Att. 6.1.1

    In the entry for receive

  • gallīnam ut ā tē missam libenter accēpī

    I was glad to receive the hen, as it came from youPlin. Ep. 7.21.4

    Here, take it.Traupman 389
